title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III
summary: Two large-scale 40.6 cm x 94 cm cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabric samples burned in a 30 cm/s air flow (concurrent and opposed) aboard an uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft to investigate low-gravity fire growth and spread rates.

tests.notes: Thickness reported as .33 cm (= 3.3 mm) in source table; typical SIBAL fabric is ~0.33 mm to 0.37 mm, so this may be a unit typo in the PSI table. O2 and pressure not reported in table; assumed nominal ISS cabin conditions (21% O2, 101.3 kPa). Sensor telemetry shows initial O2 ~19.9% and pressure ~14.4 psia (~99.3 kPa). Complete burn inferred from thermocouple cascade and radiometer heat flux across the entire sample length.

Thickness reported as .33 cm (= 3.3 mm) in source table; typical SIBAL fabric is ~0.33 mm to 0.37 mm, so this may be a unit typo in the PSI table. O2 and pressure not reported in table; assumed nominal ISS cabin conditions (21% O2, 101.3 kPa). Sensor telemetry shows initial O2 ~19.8% and pressure ~14.4 psia (~99.3 kPa). Partial burn inferred from radiometer activation between t=68s and t=132s, plume temp rise, and test termination when flow stopped at t=130s before downstream thermocouples reached elevated temperatures.
